title: session-stabilizer: tenant-session-quarantine-and-transparent-fallback-for-private-runtime-upgrades
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: During private (VPC) runtime upgrades we see disruption for long-lived sessions and streaming clients (gRPC/WS). Current rolling strategies move traffic but do not stabilize in-flight session state: clients reconnect, KV-cache priming is lost for some tenants, and customer-facing tail latency spikes. This ticket proposes a Session Stabilizer pattern — a quarantine + transparent-fallback mechanism combined with IaC hooks — to enable zero-downtime upgrades while preserving tenant session continuity and reducing rollback incidents.

Scope: implement controller-side changes and Terraform module updates to create a temporary quarantine pool for new runtime instances, a transparent fallback proxy that maintains session affinity during transitions, synthetic traffic priming for per-tenant caches, enhanced health-probing surface, and rollback automation triggers based on SLO/metrics. This work targets Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments ONLY. Hosted API rollout remains unchanged.

Why this is different: instead of larger canaries or immediate traffic shifting, the Session Stabilizer isolates new nodes behind a tenant-aware quarantine so KV and model caches can be primed with tenant-shaped synthetic requests, while live client sessions are mirrored to a transparent fallback that preserves socket/session continuity. The approach reduces noisy neighbor effects and makes rollback deterministic (evacuate quarantine + cutover to previous pool) with minimal user-visible error.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module changes provision an opt-in 'quarantine' ASG/instance group and expose flags for quarantine size and priming duration
Runtime controller supports a quarantine lifecycle: PREPARE -> PRIME -> HEALTHY -> PROMOTE -> OBSERVE; states are visible in Console and via metrics

A transparent fallback proxy (sidecar or edge) preserves long-lived TCP/Websocket/gRPC sessions during instance rotation and can mirror traffic to quarantine nodes for priming without impacting production requests
Automated rollback triggers exist and are tested: 5xx spike > 2x baseline for 3m, p95 latency regression > 30% for 5m, or synthetic-priming failure for > 2 attempts
End-to-end test in staging that simulates 500 long-lived streaming clients shows no more than 0.5% session failures during a full runtime upgrade
Runbook for manual intervention and rollback validated with on-call and customer success teams
Metrics and dashboards added to Console: quarantine size, priming success rate, mirrored-session throughput, session-failure-rate, rollback-trigger-fires
implementation_steps: Design: finalize quarantine lifecycle state machine and fallback proxy semantics (API + controller contract) — doc at https://confluence.redwood/infradev/session-stabilizer (draft)
Terraform: add 'quarantine' submodule to private-runtime module with vars: quarantine_capacity, priming_policy, health_probe_profile
Controller: implement quarantine lifecycle controller and Prometheus metrics; expose feature flag 'session_stabilizer=true' per deployment
Proxy: build lightweight transparent fallback as option (ADAPT existing edge-proxy) with connection mirroring and sticky session token support
Priming: add synthetic priming harness that runs tenant-shaped workloads against quarantine nodes and records cache-warm metrics
Health checks: extend probes to include priming-success and app-level readiness beyond simple TCP/HTTP
Rollback automation: add policy engine rules (thresholds) that trigger automatic quarantine evacuation and traffic cutback to previous pool; create safety cooldown
Terraform + Operator integration tests in CI: simulate deployment with feature flag on, validate metrics and rollback rules
Staging rollout: run staged rollout in customer-like staging VPC with chaos testing (network flaps, partial saturations)
Docs/Console: add UI for quarantine config, status, and single-click abort/rollback
test_plan: Unit tests for controller state transitions and policy evaluation
Integration test: deploy feature-flagged runtime to staging VPC, launch 500 streaming clients, perform rolling upgrade, assert session-failure-rate < 0.5%
Load test: priming harness warms per-tenant caches for 100 synthetic tenants with realistic token distributions
Chaos tests: drop 10% of quarantine nodes mid-priming to ensure controller retries and backoff work
Metric-based rollback test: induce synthetic latency to trigger rollback rule and verify evacuation path works and no new sessions are routed to quarantine
runbook: 1) If rollout health degrades, set feature-flag 'session_stabilizer=false' to prevent new quarantines
2) Check quarantine metrics: priming_success_rate, mirrored_session_errors, promoted_ready_count
3) If automated rollback triggered: notify on-call, evacuate quarantine pool (controller drains primed nodes), and shift traffic to previous stable pool
4) For manual rollback: run terraform apply with previous module version and set operator to 'evacuate_and_deactivate_quarantine=true'
5) Post-incident: gather logs (proxy, controller, priming harness), open postmortem and attach to this ticket
comments: 2026-03-02 — Aisha Raman: Created ticket after observing repeated session drops during two customer private upgrades last month. Proposed quarantine + transparent fallback to avoid cold-cache-induced rollbacks.

2026-03-04 — Architecture review: suggested replacing full sidecar with an opt-in transparent edge mode to reduce per-instance overhead. Decision: implement both paths; start with edge proxy for dedicated nodes.
2026-03-06 — Security review kickoff: security team requested threat model for connection mirroring and session tokens; assigned to security review ticket SEC-412 (link in Confluence doc).
2026-03-08 — Dev notes (Liam O'Connor): Prototype controller state machine implemented in branch ENG-137642-controller-prototype. Basic PREPARE -> PRIME -> HEALTHY transitions work in local e2e.
2026-03-10 — QA: staging integration failed initial priming run due to priming harness not handling tenant rate-limits; fixed harness to respect tenant-level throttles (PR #847).
2026-03-12 — PM (Elena Park): Approved target schedule for March release candidate pending successful chaos tests. Requesting visibility in Console for quarantine status by next week.
